title: Show the effective landing and gate policy in the JetBrains settings dialog
description:
Roadmap 2026-09-10 §4 "Effective settings" and the Wave 0 row "legacy policy cleanup". The settings dialog advertises a landing policy the wrappers do not implement, so what the user reads there does not describe what happens to their code.

moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt:20 `data class ProjectSettings` exposes exactly eight fields, three of which no longer drive anything: autoCreateBranch, branchPattern (default "moe/{epicId}/{taskId}") and commitPattern (default "feat({epicId}): {taskTitle}"). Real landing in scripts/moe-agent.{ps1,sh} never creates a branch per task; it peels onto the literal settings.consolidationBranch, else the shared moe/work-YYYY-MM-DD, reusing an existing non-default branch. Completion commit subjects are feat|fix(task-<id>): <title> and checkpoints are wip(task-<id>): ... — neither derives from commitPattern. Meanwhile every setting that does govern outcomes is absent from the dialog: autoCommit, checkpointCommits, checkpointPush, consolidationBranch, commitBoardState, commitHooks, qualityGate, attribution.undeclared and taskSizing.

Scope: stop presenting the three dead fields as live policy, and render the settings that actually decide whether a task's bytes reach a branch. Read them from the daemon's project settings with the same defaults the daemon applies, so a project that has never written a key still shows the effective value rather than a blank. Read-only display is enough; making them editable is out of scope. Do not touch the deprecated task time-budget UI, which is the separate sibling task in this epic.
definitionOfDone: autoCreateBranch, branchPattern and commitPattern are removed from the settings dialog, or clearly labelled as ignored legacy keys that no longer affect landing

The dialog shows the effective landing policy: autoCommit, checkpointCommits, checkpointPush, consolidationBranch (with the shared moe/work-YYYY-MM-DD fallback named), commitBoardState and commitHooks
The dialog shows the effective quality-gate scope and the attribution.undeclared mode
Values absent from .moe/project.json render the daemon's default rather than blank or false, with a JUnit test covering both the populated and the all-defaults case
The JUnit test fails on the old behaviour (today the dialog renders branchPattern and commitPattern as live settings)
docs/CONFIGURATION.md matches the labels shown, and no longer implies branch-per-task landing
taskRails: Read-only surface: do not make these settings editable from the dialog and do not add a settings-write path.
Do not touch the deprecated time-budget UI — that is the sibling task in this epic; overlapping edits will collide.
Defaults must match packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts, which is the source of truth for settings defaults.

implementationPlan.description:
Parse the new settings in MoeJson with the daemon's exact default semantics and total error handling.

In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt, `parseProjectSettings`:
- Drop the `autoCreateBranch` / `branchPattern` / `commitPattern` lines.
- Add a private helper `getStrictBooleanOrDefault(obj: JsonObject, key: String, default: Boolean): Boolean` that returns the value ONLY when the element is a JSON boolean primitive (`element.isJsonPrimitive && element.asJsonPrimitive.isBoolean`), and the default for absent, null, or any non-boolean. This is not cosmetic: the existing `getBooleanOrDefault` calls Gson's `asBoolean`, which on the JSON string "no" returns false via `Boolean.parseBoolean`, while the daemon's `"no" !== false` evaluates to TRUE. The strict helper reproduces `!== false` (default true) and `=== true` (default false) for every JSON shape. Leave the existing `getBooleanOrDefault` and its callers untouched.
- `autoCommit`, `checkpointCommits`, `checkpointPush`, `commitBoardState`: `getStrictBooleanOrDefault(settings, key, true)`.
- `commitHooks`: `getStrictBooleanOrDefault(settings, "commitHooks", false)`.
- `consolidationBranch` and `qualityGate`: `settings.getStringOrDefault(key, "").trim()`.
- `qualityGateScope`: `settings.getStringOrDefault("qualityGateScope", "epicFinal")` clamped with `.takeIf { it in setOf("epicFinal", "everyTask") } ?: "epicFinal"`, matching the `approvalMode` clamp two lines above and the wrapper's own fallback.
- `attributionUndeclared`: read the nested `attribution` object (guard `isJsonObject`, else an empty JsonObject), then `getStringOrDefault("undeclared", "solo")` clamped to {solo, never, always} with `solo` as the fallback.
- `taskSizing`: add `private fun parseTaskSizing(settingsJson: JsonObject): TaskSizingThresholds` next to `parseColumnLimits`. Read the nested `taskSizing` object (guard `isJsonObject`, else empty). Each value must be a POSITIVE int or the default is used — mirror planSize.ts `positiveInt`: use `getIntOrNull(key)?.takeIf { it > 0 } ?: default`. Then apply planSize.ts's inversion guard: `maxSteps = maxOf(warnSteps, rawMaxSteps)` and `maxDistinctFiles = maxOf(warnDistinctFiles, rawMaxDistinctFiles)`, so a partial settings edit cannot render an inverted band.

The error handling contract for this whole function: `.moe/project.json` is hand-editable, so no reader may throw. Every new read guards its JSON type before touching it and falls back to the daemon default, exactly as the existing helpers wrap `asInt`/`asString` in try/catch. A malformed settings block must degrade to defaults, never crash the state parse and blank the board.
implementationPlan.note:
parseProjectSettings rewritten per plan. Dropped the three legacy reads; added the ten new ones.

New private helper getStrictBooleanOrDefault(obj, key, default) returns the value only when `element.isJsonPrimitive && asJsonPrimitive.isBoolean`, else the default — reproducing the daemon's `!== false` (default true) and `=== true` (default false) for every JSON shape. Existing getBooleanOrDefault and its two remaining callers (approvalMode-adjacent enableAgentTeams, plus the task-parsing callers) untouched, per plan.

autoCommit/checkpointCommits/checkpointPush/commitBoardState -> strict true; commitHooks -> strict false. consolidationBranch/qualityGate -> getStringOrDefault(key, "").trim(). qualityGateScope clamped to {epicFinal, everyTask} else epicFinal, same shape as the approvalMode clamp above it. attribution read as a type-guarded nested object (else empty JsonObject) then undeclared clamped to {solo, never, always} else solo.

New private fun parseTaskSizing(settingsJson) sits next to parseColumnLimits: type-guarded nested taskSizing object, each value `getIntOrNull(key)?.takeIf { it > 0 } ?: default` (planSize.ts positiveInt), then maxSteps = maxOf(warnSteps, raw) and maxDistinctFiles = maxOf(warnDistinctFiles, raw) (planSize.ts inversion guard).

Error handling verified by re-reading the helpers rather than assuming: getStringOrDefault (MoeJson.kt:41) already returns the default for a null/absent/non-primitive element inside a try/catch, and getIntOrNull (MoeJson.kt:71) wraps asInt the same way — so no new read can throw on a hand-corrupted project.json. Added a KDoc on parseProjectSettings stating that contract and one on parseTaskSizing naming planSize.ts.

Added `import com.moe.model.TaskSizingThresholds` alphabetically between TaskMetrics and TaskVerification. Deliberately did NOT touch the TaskBudget import or any task-parsing code — that region belongs to sibling task-435683c2df8f47e.

implementationPlan.description:
Add the pure, headless-testable row builder plus its test — this is the step whose test fails on the old behaviour.

In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/MoeSettingsDialog.kt add a `companion object` (same convention as `CreateTaskDialog.epicSelectionModel` and `MetricsPanel.firstPassApprovalText`, both of which are already unit-tested headlessly in this module):
- `data class PolicyRow(val label: String, val value: String, val detail: String = "")`.
- `fun effectivePolicyRows(settings: ProjectSettings?): List<PolicyRow>` returning, in this order, from `settings ?: ProjectSettings()` — the null coalesce is deliberate error handling for a board that has not received a snapshot yet, so the dialog shows daemon defaults instead of a blank panel:
  1. "Auto-commit" — On/Off. detail: on = "Every session exit lands this task's attributed paths."; off = "No completion, checkpoint or rescue commits."
  2. "Checkpoint commits" — On/Off. detail names the `wip(task-<id>)` subject.
  3. "Push checkpoints" — On/Off. detail: off = "Checkpoints stay local."
  4. "Commit board state" — On/Off. detail names `.moe/tasks/<id>.json`.
  5. "Commit hooks" — "Run on completion commits" / "Skipped (plumbing commits)".
  6. "Landing branch" — three cases, all tested: empty -> value "moe/work-<YYYY-MM-DD> (shared, default)" with detail "No consolidationBranch set; wrappers peel onto the shared dated branch."; a literal value -> that value, detail "Peel target and the branch complete_task requires."; a value containing `*` -> that value, detail "Glob checked at complete_task only; wrappers still peel onto moe/work-<YYYY-MM-DD>." The glob distinction is real (see docs/CONFIGURATION.md `consolidationBranch` and the `ensure_safe_branch`/`peel_target_branch` comment in scripts/moe-agent.sh: only a literal doubles as the peel target). Render the literal placeholder text "moe/work-<YYYY-MM-DD>" — do NOT compute today's date, so the row is stable and the test is not time-dependent.
  7. "Quality gate" — empty -> "Disabled (no command configured)"; else the command string.
  8. "Quality gate scope" — "epicFinal" -> "Epic-final task only"; "everyTask" -> "Every task".
  9. "Undeclared-file attribution" — solo -> "Commit when no other worker is live (solo)"; never -> "Declared files only (never)"; always -> "Always commit (always)".
  10. "Plan size limits" — "Warn past N steps / M files, reject past P / Q" from the four thresholds.

Use plain Kotlin strings, NOT MoeBundle, for these labels and values. `MoeBundle` wraps `DynamicBundle`, which needs an application instance the plain-JUnit `test` task does not create (build.gradle.kts strips the IntelliJ platform argument provider), and no existing test calls it. `MetricsPanel.firstPassApprovalText` sets the precedent of a hardcoded display string tested directly.

Assert no row `value` is blank.
- `populated settings render their configured values`: build a ProjectSettings with everything non-default and assert each row's value.
- `an unset consolidation branch names the shared dated fallback`, `a literal consolidation branch is the peel target`, `a glob consolidation branch is check-only`: three focused tests on row 6.
- `no row presents the retired branch or commit pattern settings`: assert that the concatenation of every label+value+detail contains none of "branchPattern", "commitPattern", "Branch Pattern", "Commit Pattern", "{epicId}", "{taskId}", "{taskTitle}", "Auto-create git branches".
- One end-to-end test that feeds a raw daemon snapshot JSON with NO `settings` key through `MoeJson.parseState`, takes `state.project.settings`, and passes it to `effectivePolicyRows`, asserting the same all-defaults rows. This proves the DoD's "absent from .moe/project.json renders the daemon default" across the real parse path rather than a hand-built object.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Labelling the three dead fields as legacy in the dialog versus removing them: the Definition of Done allows either. Removal wins because leaving three inert editable text fields on a read-only policy screen invites someone to type into them, and the daemon merge means the typed value would silently persist while changing nothing.

Putting the row builder in a new top-level object versus a companion on the dialog: the companion matches the two existing tested helpers in this module and keeps the distinct-file count down. The plan names the top-level-object extraction as the fallback if class init misbehaves under the platform-free test JVM.

Including taskSizing: the task description lists it among the settings that govern outcomes, but the Definition of Done does not name it. It is included as a single derived row because it is cheap and the description calls it out; if a reviewer disagrees it is one row to delete, not a structural change. taskSizing is the only item in that description list not required by the Definition of Done.

Updating moe-vscode in the same task: rejected. The epic rail says JetBrains ships first and VS Code follows in the same task only if trivial. moe-vscode/src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts is a webview with its own HTML and message-passing surface and its own test pattern, which is not trivial. It needs a follow-up card.

DEFAULT SOURCE OF TRUTH. The task rail names packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts, but that file only seeds a fresh project.json (approvalMode, speedModeDelayMs, autoCreateBranch, branchPattern, commitPattern, agentCommand, enableAgentTeams, chatEnabled, chatMaxAgentHops) and defines NO default for any landing or gate setting. The daemon applies those defaults at read time instead, in the policy block of packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts: autoCommit/checkpointCommits/checkpointPush/commitBoardState are `settings.X !== false` (default true), commitHooks is `settings.commitHooks === true` (default false), attribution.undeclared is `?? 'solo'`. qualityGateScope defaults to epicFinal in the wrapper's own fallback in scripts/moe-agent.sh. Plan-size thresholds default 8/12/5/10 in packages/moe-daemon/src/util/planSize.ts, with a max-lifted-to-warn guard. The plan uses those, which is what the rail intends.

BOOLEAN PARITY IS THE SUBTLE PART. The daemon's `!== false` treats every non-boolean value as true. Gson's asBoolean on a JSON string calls Boolean.parseBoolean, so the existing MoeJson getBooleanOrDefault would turn "no" into false where the daemon says true. Step 2 adds a strict boolean reader that only honours a real JSON boolean; the existing helper stays for the settings that already use it.

SAVE CANNOT CLOBBER. validateSettingsUpdate in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/validators.ts builds `next` from `{ ...project.settings }` and only overwrites keys present in the incoming payload, so dropping the three retired keys from the MoeCommandSender payload leaves any stored value intact. The allowlist in that same function still accepts all three, so no daemon change is needed.

HEADLESS TEST CONVENTION. moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts strips the IntelliJ platform argument provider from the `test` task, so tests run on a bare JVM with JUnit 4. CreateTaskDialogTest already calls a companion function on a DialogWrapper subclass and MetricsPanelTest asserts a hardcoded display string, so both patterns are proven here. MoeBundle wraps DynamicBundle and is called by no test — keep it out of the pure row builder.

CONSOLIDATION BRANCH SEMANTICS. Only a LITERAL consolidationBranch doubles as the wrapper's peel target (ensure_safe_branch / peel_target_branch in scripts/moe-agent.sh); a `*` glob is checked at complete_task only and the wrapper still peels onto moe/work-<date>. Rendering both cases identically would repeat exactly the kind of lie this task exists to remove.
